literal: To affliction, affliction they will inflict, who to affliction do not suffer.
translation: Those who do not lose heart and suffer when affliction comes will themselves inflict affliction upon that affliction.
modern: துன்பம் வரும்போது அதற்காக வருந்தாதவர்கள், அந்தத் துன்பத்திற்கே துன்பத்தை உண்டாக்குவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of resilience in the face of adversity. The poet uses a powerful repetition of the word 'idumbai' (affliction) to illustrate a psychological triumph. When a person refuses to be broken or saddened by difficulties, they effectively disarm the trouble itself. Instead of the individual suffering, the distress is defeated and forced to retreat, meaning the resilient person inflicts suffering upon the suffering itself.
